headline: Use membership to remember every distinct value
statement: Return true if any integer occurs at least twice in nums; otherwise return false.
intuition: When you see a number again, the earlier copy is all the evidence needed. A set forgets order and frequency, which are irrelevant here, while retaining efficient membership checks.
approach: For each value, return true if it is already present.
Otherwise add it and continue; return false after the scan.
correctness: Before processing each value, seen contains exactly the values at earlier indices. Membership therefore detects precisely a pair with the current index as its later endpoint. If no membership succeeds, all values occur once.
bruteForce: Compare every pair of indices, which can require O(n²) comparisons.

complexity.explanation: Hash-set membership and insertion take expected constant time, giving expected O(n) runtime. The expectation concerns performance, not correctness. At most n distinct values are retained.

pitfalls: Do not assume duplicates are adjacent.
Negative numbers and zero are ordinary set keys.
